finding:
Partial landing. Given a second-countable R_{>0}-modulated G and a nonempty real interval I, the printed fourth bullet calls S_I(G) a strict LF-space, nuclear, complete and Montel, in the locally convex inductive limit of the weighted-map stages on G/k from the preceding bullet. Its examples of uses do not assert bounded lifting for arbitrary quotients of nuclear spaces. It gives no proof. Theorem D.3.3.7(2) explicitly assumes a continuous homomorphic section of the surjective module (compare the section construction claimed in Remark D.2.1.2). Example D.3.3.5 argues for nuclear Fréchet stages using the endpoint and then countable closed embeddings, and for strictness using the unweighted stage embeddings; the proof of (2) invokes permanence under countable strict inductive limits, not (1)'s tensor-product identification. Definition D.3.3.3 starts with compact generation in the full dual but its inductive-limit paragraph says finite generation. These are not interchangeable there: the full annihilator contains the uncountable radial dual, whereas p. 804 gives the intended equivalent finite-generation condition in the discrete dual of G^1. The result here does not silently use the literal full-dual finite-generation indexing.

The new Lean results prove the radial Fréchet step for the actual Masullo.logWeightedStage I, i.e. the identity-module case G = R_{>0}, k = 1 in logarithmic coordinates, not a substitute topology. The prior accepted receipt a24169779b63b6bb698aaee9624851661731e359204e44224fb341f733aca414-707d3975dcd53b08d0cd0590f7ab595af0d0a2bb6ca5b27f11dd553a284dcce7 and its Proofs/Theorems/RadialWeightedSchwartzStage.lean give the common-profile range and completeness in the product-induced uniformity, not metrizability. Differentiating the global change-of-weight identity exp((c−a)x) F_a(x) = F_c(x) by Leibniz and using a on x ≤ 0 and b on x ≥ 0 yields an explicit finite bound for each Schwartz seminorm at a ≤ c ≤ b, with coefficients depending only on the weights and derivative order. The theorem works for any stage element and does not assume that 0 is a weight. It controls convergence at zero in each original coordinate, so any bracketing subset induces the original uniformity, not just an injective restriction. A countable dense subset of I together with any attained extrema brackets every weight, including for singleton and nonclosed I. For nonempty I this restriction is a closed embedding by the accepted completeness result. The inherited uniformity is countably generated and metrizable, and the inherited complex vector topology is locally convex over the underlying real scalars. Thus with existing completeness it is a radial Fréchet stage, with a complete compatible metric; this does not prove radial nuclearity or Montel. The bound is for tuples already in the common-profile stage; it does not by itself construct a stage element from arbitrary pairs of endpoint inputs.

No general quotient-stage identification, cofinal subgroup system, transition strictness, strict LF topology, nuclearity, completeness of the general limit, or Montel result is established. The accepted continuousMulEquivOfSection in Proofs/Lemmas/ContinuousNormSplit.lean needs a given section; the rational additive stages in Proofs/Props/RationalAdeleStageTransition.lean and Proofs/Props/RationalAdeleSchwartzLF.lean are not the weighted modulated quotients in the bullet. See .godel/formalize/radial-weighted-frechet.md for the scope comparison and rerunnable ordinary-import checks.
